objective: Review the definition-only execution boundary after the accepted direct command-path native-invocation fixture, decide whether a later run gate may attempt a scoped real Verilator-facing native invocation proof, and keep this review from claiming native option support, direct Verilator command execution, sidecar execution by this gate, compare execution, measured timing, speedup, arbitrary filelist support, automatic GPU allocation, runtime/ABI change, raw full-state equality, or production LLM-serving throughput.

review_decision.reason: The definition is narrow enough for a later scoped run gate because it admits only accepted native-invocation fixture metadata as input, requires a real built or reviewed Verilator process parse result before native execution can be claimed, keeps fixture argv, parser payload, wrapper execution, generated command text, and materialized stage-plan metadata out of runtime authority, requires explicit sidecar context plus reviewed stage authority before any sidecar stage can execute, constrains generated evidence to reports/ and artifacts/, and keeps coverage_output_equivalence as future compare evidence only.
review_decision.weakest_point: The reviewed boundary still has not executed a real native Verilator command. The name can look stronger than the evidence: it only approves a later run gate to prove process-level parsing and scoped sidecar execution. It does not prove upstream Verilator support, arbitrary filelist handling, automatic allocation, timing, speedup, coverage-output equivalence, runtime/ABI change, raw full-state equality, or production throughput.
